findings.issue_text: Boundary drift between shards 1 and 2: repos.go's resolveRepos classifies an existing clone whose fetch or rev-parse failed as 'missing' (pinned to nothing), but main.go's report can only see pass.rev(URL)=="" and files such claims under the 'no-clone' matrix row. The per-claim disclosure does name '(fetch failed)', and the rollup excludes the row either way, so the conflation only slightly mislabels the row for operators; severity low, documented trade-off, non-blocking.

evidence.note: accepted risk: pin-failed clones are named in the missing disclosure with a (fetch failed) suffix, distinguishable from absent clones; the no-clone row aggregates them, disclosed per URL

findings.issue_text: Escalation seam re-runs RepoTestEvidence instead of reusing the executor's memoized search (explicitly documented in the file as deliberate: escalation resolves lazily before the executor may have searched). Transient seam failure between the primary arm and the escalation materialization could give the second-opinion tree fewer repo evidence paths than the primary prompt displayed; both arms fail open identically and the pinned rev is the same, so divergence is bounded and rare; severity low, non-blocking.

evidence.note: accepted risk: the escalation seam re-runs the search rather than reusing the executor memo, documented as deliberate at this site because escalation resolves before the executor may have searched
grep across repo: no remaining callers of removed gitCtx; no stale 4-arg ContextForGapClaim callers; both GrepSeam/ShowSeam call sites delegate to the single shared implementation
shard-0 golden prompt fixtures and shard-3 RubricAddendum text are character-identical, keeping the prompt-rubric golden tests in lockstep across shards
